claim.quote: We establish the existence of the top quark using a 67 pb^-1 data sample of Pbar-P collisions at Sqrt(s) = 1.8 TeV collected with the Collider Detector at Fermilab (CDF).

date.note: Public announcement date; the PRL paper (74, 2626) itself was arXiv-submitted 1995-03-02/03 (hep-ex/9503002) and formally published later in 1995 without a stated month on INSPIRE.
date.quote: On March 2, 1995, physicists at CDF and DZero announced the discovery of the top quark.

key_value_text.quote: inconsistent with the background prediction by 4.8 sigma
key_value_text.value: Signal inconsistent with background-only by 4.8 sigma; reconstructed top mass measured (paper reports 176 GeV region, not exactly reproduced here)

name: Observation of Top Quark Production in ppbar Collisions with the Collider Detector at Fermilab
notes: result_type is "observation" (not "discovery") because that is the paper's own title/abstract wording, per instructions to follow the collaboration's wording rather than press characterizations (Fermilab's own tevatron/experiments pages call this "the discovery of the top quark", but the PRL 74, 2626 title and abstract say "Observation ...\"/"We establish the existence...").

title/name corrected in a 2026-09-17 verification pass: the record previously read "Observation of top quark production in ppbar collisions", dropping the published title's "with the Collider Detector at Fermilab" clause and its capitalisation; confirmed verbatim against journals.aps.org/prl/abstract/10.1103/PhysRevLett.74.2626, whose title is "Observation of Top Quark Production in pbar-p Collisions with the Collider Detector at Fermilab" (rendered here with the repository's ASCII "ppbar" convention).

significance.quote: inconsistent with the background prediction by 4.8 sigma

summary.plain: In 1995, the CDF experiment announced it had found clear evidence of the top quark, the heaviest and last of the six quarks predicted by the Standard Model, using collisions at Fermilab's Tevatron.
summary.technical: CDF observation of top-quark pair production in ppbar collisions at sqrt(s)=1.8 TeV using a 67 pb^-1 sample; a signal consistent with t-tbar -> WWbbbar decay, inconsistent with background by 4.8 sigma, with a corroborating peak in the reconstructed mass distribution.

title: Observation of Top Quark Production in ppbar Collisions with the Collider Detector at Fermilab
why_it_matters: The top quark was the last of the six quarks of the Standard Model to be found; establishing its existence and mass let physicists test the internal consistency of the Standard Model and, later, constrain the Higgs boson mass.
